done_when: The commit hook refuses only when git commit itself is given -n or --no-verify, never for an -n that belongs to another command on the same line

findings.body: Raise: Security. The heredoc matcher at line 208 treats `<< 2` in `echo $((1 << 2))` as a heredoc opener. It then discards a following `git commit -n` line while searching for a line containing only `2`, so the hook permits a command that skips Git hooks. It also reads `<<E"OF"` as a heredoc ending at `E` rather than `EOF`, which can discard a prohibited commit after the real heredoc ends.
findings.title: Arithmetic left shift or a partly quoted delimiter can hide a prohibited commit

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The shell check at lines 219–221 restores every heredoc body if an earlier command invokes `bash`. For `bash -c true && git commit -F - <<'EOF'` followed by a message line mentioning `git commit -n`, the hook inspects that message as a command and refuses the commit, although the commit has neither prohibited option. The named allowed tests do not put a shell command before a commit whose message mentions `-n`.
